newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China takes 50,000t soybeans, 100,000t more coming.
newsitem.headline: China takes 50,000t soybeans, 100,000t more coming.

text.p: A cargo of 50,000 tonnes of soybeans from South America has arrived in the northern Chinese port of Dalian, a source at the city's commodity exchange told Reuters on Friday.
"The beans are from Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay," the source said by telephone. He said the cargo arrived on Wednesday.
Another shipment of 100,000 tonnes of soybeans was expected for delivery to China in mid-September, industry sources said in Beijing and Dalian.

"Of that, 50,000 tonnes are for delivery to the Dalian Commodity Exchange against futures contracts, and 50,000 tonnes for delivery elsewhere," said one trade source, citing a Chinese government official.
That shipment could be from the United States, the sources said, but were unable to confirm the origin.
In a report issued on Thursday, the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) said exporters had reported 108,500 tonnes of soybean sales to China in the week ending August 22.
The figure included 105,900 tonnes switched to China from an unknown destination, the report said.
According to the USDA, accumulated soybean exports to China this year, as of August 22, reached 422,800 tonnes.
